For each tetrahedron $t$, iterate over its four vertices $v$ [S1, S2, unofficial].

The claim states that for each tetrahedron $t$, one iterates over its four vertices $v$. The evidence in both S1 and S2 explicitly defines the error function for a tetrahedron $t$ as the maximum over all vertices $v$ in $t$ (i.e., $v$ is a vertex of $t$). Since a tetrahedron has exactly four vertices, computing the maximum over all vertices $v$ in $t$ inherently involves iterating over or considering all four vertices. The evidence confirms that the error is computed based on these four vertices.

This confirms that the method involves evaluating vertices from the source grid V within the context of the PRI P to compute the error.

The formula is $\text{Total Error} = \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{R_i - R_r}{R_r}$, where $n$ is the number of triangles multiplied by 3, $R_i$ is the distance from the sphere center to vertex $i$ (denoted $r_i$ in the source), and $R_r$ is the reference sphere radius [S3, unofficial].

The claim states that $R_i$ is the distance from the sphere center to vertex $i$. However, the evidence explicitly states that '$R_i$ is the radius of the sphere' and '$R_r$ is the distance from the center ... to a vertex'. The claim swaps the definitions of $R_i$ and $R_r$ compared to the source text.
